title: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

sense.text:
We are in some dark times, and the Lord has been showing us, but we don’t catch it. “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times”: the moon serves in a season for a declaration of time.

“And a sign of the world”: that’s the part right there. The moon symbolizes a sign of the world we live in. Put up the phases of the moon: what they call a full moon is actually the new moon. It goes from bright, and phases all the way to dark, decreasing; then it begins to increase again.

“A light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The new moon is bright, in her perfection. When was the earth in its perfection? During the time of Adam. Then it begins to decrease, and darkness begins to cover it till it gets black.

When the moon is dark, that represents sin and Satan and all the wickedness, Edom and all the wickedness that we see taking place.

So what have we learned? The moon is a declaration of times, a sign of the world; it’s symbolic of the world. It started out in its perfection and it decreased until it gets dark, as we read in Isaiah 60:2. Then after Esau, who comes? Brothers, Jacob, like we read, and it begins to go right back. That’s what the moon symbolizes.

precepts.why: “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is the world during the time of Adam: back then it brought forth immortality. That is the moon in her perfection, bright and full.

“For look how much the world shall be weaker through age, so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.” Weaker through age means time: the more time goes by on this earth, the more evils will increase. That is the light decreasing from her perfection.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The earth is going to be in total darkness, just like a phase of the moon when it goes black.

“For the world hath lost his youth, and the times begin to wax old.” “For the world is divided into twelve parts”: the angel is telling Ezra to look at the earth like a clock. Twelve parts on the clock, “and the ten parts of it are gone already”: ten o’clock, gone already, “and half of a tenth part”: that’s the 10:30 mark.

This was back then, during the time of Ezra, the time of Persia and Media, that the angel was telling him this. “And there remaineth that which is after the half of the tenth part”: from that time, all that’s left is an hour and a half. That is the moon as a declaration of times.

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other”: that’s Christ speaking. “By me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first”: when shall be the end of the first world, “and the beginning of it that followeth?”, the beginning of the world that follows.

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Esau is the last ruling empire. That’s what it means: Esau is the end of the world.

When you hear some Israelites out there say Esau is the Arabs, no, that’s wrong. If Esau is the Arabs, that means we got to go into captivity again, and that makes no damn sense. What the hell wrong with you? The Bible says Esau will go to the moon; I don’t see no damn Arabs going up there. That’s why you don’t listen to them. Some of you women are all over the place; you listen to everybody, simple as hell. Stop listening to them; you’re gonna get lost.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: that’s the other nations. “Other question, Esdras, ask thou not.” And in case some of you watching online dispute what’s being said: shut up and listen.

“Then saw I a dream, and, behold, there came up from the sea an eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads.” The question is, who was this? Obadiah answers it: Edom, whose symbol is the eagle. Then back here: “And I saw, and, behold, she spread her wings over all the earth, and all the winds of the air blew on her”. He’s talking about the eagle in all her forms: Esau, the end of the world.

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: concerning who? Edom. “We have heard a rumour from the Lord”, and the heathen are called to “rise up against her in battle”: that’s NATO. They’re prophesied to rise up against America. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Esau greatly despised.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: put the Caucasus mountains on the screen. These are the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia, where the Khazars dwelt that we read about at the beginning of today’s lesson, the Khazars of Edomite stock that make up the Jews of today. “Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say who shall bring me down to the ground, you got to have power.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”: when they landed on the moon in 1969 they said the eagle has landed, and they have mementos all throughout the country in regards to that. So Esau’s symbol is the eagle, the same eagle Ezra saw come up from the sea.

“And I beheld, and, lo, as it were a roaring lion”: this roaring lion is Christ, “chased out of the wood”, meaning it ran out of the woods. “And I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”: the voice that’s coming out is the voice of the prophets. “Hear thou, I will talk with thee, and the Highest shall say unto thee, Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” That the end of their times might come through them: this eagle would bring about the end of this time. Esau is the end of the world, the moon gone dark.

sense.text: In this spiritual darkness: right now this is a kingdom of darkness. “And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast”: upon the seed of the white man. “And his kingdom was full of darkness”: darkness shall cover the earth. “And they gnawed their tongues for pain”.

“And blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds.” They’re not going to repent. Although they see judgment coming on this earth, these people will never repent; that’s not in their spirit. Keep on waiting for your reparations.

“And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates; and the water thereof was dried up, that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.” This is what’s happening right now.

So in this kingdom of darkness, brothers and sisters, pay very close attention, because this is going to be the most important part of the class.

precepts.why:
Like Deacon Malachi said: there should never be darkness, and everything we see is dimness, darkness. You might think it’s bright outside; it ain’t bright. “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold”. We don’t see no brightness yet. We’re in the land of darkness; understand what time period you’re living in.

We’re living in the kingdom of darkness, and all of us get affected by this darkness. That’s why every day we wake up, we’re at war: put on your armor.

sense.text:
In this spiritual darkness our friends and family, and us too, all of us are in it. “And a stone of stumbling”: Christ is a stone of stumbling, “and a rock of offence”: Christ is the rock of offense. Why is he the rock of offense? Some of you get offended at the laws in the Bible, you get offended at the law, and then you blame the teachers. We’re just the messengers.

“Even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.” Some were appointed from the beginning of time: this soul will never be compliant with God’s laws. Shazam, that’s you. That’s some of your mothers, some of your fathers. We can’t change it.

“But ye are a chosen generation”: Israel, we are a chosen generation. “A royal priesthood”: brothers, we are a royal priesthood. “An holy nation”: we are a holy nation. “A peculiar people”: you’re a peculiar people, “that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness”.

We’re being called out of darkness. Remember, this is the kingdom of darkness; we’re in the final phase of the moon.

Now the question often comes up: what about my family and friends, should we cut them off? The only family and friends to cut off are those causing you to sin. Some of your mothers and fathers are not trying to get you to break the law. Some of them don’t believe and have never come to the school, but they say, okay, that’s what you believe, but we still love you, you’re our son, you’re our daughter, whatever you need we’re here to help you. Why would you cut them off? Don’t cut them off. But what about them family and friends that say, hey, let’s go sin, let’s eat some pork together?

“Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery”: read it again, one more time for the brothers online, one more time for the sisters online. Thou shalt not commit adultery.

“But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” Of course you see a woman you like, you’re gonna lust. But say you want to marry her: is there a sin in that? No, because you want to make her your wife. But say it’s a married woman, or a woman you really don’t want to marry: now you’re lusting, and that’s the sin, because all you want is wham bam thank you ma’am.

There may be people in your life, a woman that says, hey, you and me used to get it on back in the day, and she wants to rekindle that situation; or a homeboy that says, hey, remember that girl we took turns running the train on? “And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out”: that’s not literal, brothers. There’s a rapper that did rip out his eye, because the Christian church never explained what that’s talking about.

This right eye is that brother or sister that’s causing you to sin. “And cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish”: that one person that should perish is that brother or sister that’s saying, come on, let’s go back to what it used to be, let’s do it again. “And not that thy whole body should be cast into hell”: circle that; we’re gonna touch on that hell later on.

“And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off”: the right hand is still that brother or sister, friend, family or kinsman that’s trying to get you to sin. It’s offending you because he or she is saying, let’s sin. “And cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.”

“At the same time came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven? And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them, And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

This is the same thing Christ said to Nicodemus: except you be born again you cannot enter. Nicodemus said, how can I go back into my mother’s womb again? I’m an old man, I’m grown. And Christ said, are you an elder in Israel and you don’t understand this? So the same lesson Christ taught Nicodemus, the ruler of the Jews, he taught to us here in Matthew 18. “Except ye be converted”: we know what converts us is God’s law.

You can’t enter the kingdom except you be converted and become like a child: start all over again. “Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child”: humble himself to God’s laws. “The same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.” You want to be great? Humble yourself to God’s laws.
“And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.” If you accept one of them that believes in Christ, you receive Christ.

“But whoso shall offend one of these little ones”: trying to get you to sin, trying to get you to break God’s law, “which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” Christ is saying it’s better that you kill yourself. That’s what the King of Kings said: go commit suicide, go kill yourself. Wow, that’s cold; they didn’t teach me that in church.

This offense also goes into lying on each other, bearing false witness against your brother, dealing evil with your brother. That goes back to the scripture that says, how you gonna love God and hate the brother who is in front of you? You offend one of these brothers that believe in Christ, you got a price to pay for that.

“Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” For it must needs be that offenses come: we’re going to touch on why they need to come in a little bit.

“Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee”: that hand or foot is symbolic for your friend, family or neighbor. “Cut them off, and cast them from thee”. It’s better to enter into the kingdom without your friend, without your wife, without your husband, without your child, “rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.” Remember the hell we read about earlier in Matthew 5: that hell is this part here, everlasting fire.

“And if thine eye offend thee”: the eye is your mama, your daddy, your sister or brother. “Pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.” Hell fire: Moses spoke about the same thing.

precepts.why:
What converts us to becoming little children? “The law of the Lord is perfect”. Brothers and sisters, especially you men on the street, don’t get hemmed up with these stupid people that find a number in Kings, like how many horses were in Solomon’s barn, and a different number in Chronicles, or a king’s age when he began to rule in Kings and a different one in Chronicles, and say, see, imperfection, these are typos. Don’t argue about typos: oh look, Noah is spelled N-O-E over here but N-O-A-H in Genesis. Why are you arguing about that? That’s stupid.

There’s no problems with God’s law. When God says thou shalt not commit adultery, that’s perfection. When he says thou shalt not kill, that’s perfection. When he says thou shalt not bear false witness, that is perfection.

In an interview in South Africa a man asked whether the writings in the Bible are 100 percent accurate. That was a trap, so the answer was: there are some words that shouldn’t be there, like the word Easter in Acts 12. That’s a pagan term; the Israelites never celebrated that, and when you examine it the word Passover was there initially. Easter goes back to Ishtar, Esther’s name, which goes back to Ashtaroth in the book of Kings: holidays of the fertility goddess, sexuality, babies and abortions. Read from verse one through three and it tells you we were celebrating the feast of unleavened bread. Always be prepared for these people that try to hem you up.

“Converting the soul”: the law is what converts us. “The testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We got to acknowledge we’re the simple. Brother, I don’t care what kind of degree you got, you are simple. Sister, we’re the most educated generation, simple as hell. If you want to be wise you got to go to the perfection of the Lord, which is his law. Masters, doctorate or whatever, you’re simple until you come back to God’s laws.

sense.text:
Christ spoke of hell fire, and Moses spoke about the same thing. This is for the churchgoers and the Christians: “If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder”. Growing up in church there was always some woman who had a word of knowledge from God: ‘God got a message for you young man, you’re going to be a man of the Lord, you’re going to do great things.’ You see them on TV: send the money, get a prayer cloth, a word of knowledge, you’re going to get healed. There was a famous dude to the stars, always with a word of knowledge, a word of wisdom, God showed him something about the rich and famous.

It sounds like this: ‘I had a dream about you the other night,’ or ‘I had a vision that you’re going to get a job on the third Wednesday of October.’

“And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them”. Once that sign or wonder comes to pass they convince you. They won’t say ‘other gods’, they’ll say ‘let’s go worship Jesus, come on to my church’, Baptist, Mormon, Episcopal, Anglican: ‘that dream, that vision I had toward you, that’s from the Lord, let’s go worship him.’

“Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams”. Why not? “For the Lord your God proveth you”: God is testing you, “to know whether ye love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.”

“Ye shall walk after the Lord your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments”. If the dream or the vision that comes to pass is trying to get you to go against God’s commandments, that’s how you know it’s false. It’s not of the Lord. God is testing you, proving you.

“And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death”: under Moses’ law he or she was to be put to death, “because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God”. Their whole objective was to get you to worship a false god.

People ask, why did God do this, the brother’s or the sister’s vision or dream came to pass? Dummy, have you not been reading your four chapters a day? Study, pray, apply. You’ve been warned: reading four chapters a day you had to come across Deuteronomy 13. Your mama had a dream, your bishop or your priest had a dream or a vision about you, and the job came, the money came, the marriage came, the baby came. Some of these women can’t get pregnant and they’re told, you’re going to get pregnant next month, the 14th day of November, and now she’s pregnant. The Lord allowed all that to happen, because now they say: come on to church, come worship white jesus, you ain’t got to keep no law. And you go, okay. You have just failed the test, and now it’s hell fire for your black behind.

This verse goes with Matthew 18:8 and Matthew 5, the hand, the foot and the eye. “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul”: it’s as if they’re a part of you. You grew up with them, you love them so intensely, it’s as if they’re a part of you, like an eye, like a hand, like a foot.

“Or thy son, or thy daughter”: you women read that. Believe it or not, some people have left the truth at the behest of their children: ‘mommy, daddy, I don’t want to be here,’ and out of love for that child mommy and daddy left the truth. True stories; there are a million of them.

“Or the wife of thy bosom”: you brothers can be strong, but when you get married the real you will come out. He was always a simp; he just put on a good show. Marry a woman and love her beyond God, and the real simp nature comes out, seeping through your pores, and you stand up for wickedness. There’s a recent story of a brother, an officer in New York, speaking up on behalf of a rebellious girl that was just put out, saying we judged her wrong. In Florida, at one of our schools, the scripture says the woman shall not wear what man wears, and the sister told her husband, ‘I got a spandex dress, men don’t wear this,’ and he said, ‘I love you so much babe, you’re right.’ She walked her behind into the school in a spandex dress so tight her feet could only go so far in front of each other, and the captain said, ‘what the hell do y’all think y’all doing,’ and thank God the captain threw both of them out that night. Those are the v-o-g brothers: brothers that put vagina over God.

“Or thy friend”: some of you come in here for friendship, and your friend falls out of the truth and you fall out with him. You’re simple as hell. Every man was called into this truth alone. You were born alone, you’re gonna die alone.

“Entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods”: they won’t necessarily say those words. They’ll say, ‘hey, let’s go commit adultery; I know the god you serve says thou shalt not commit adultery, but my god says thou shalt commit adultery.’ That is what Matthew 5 was talking about: cut it off, pluck your eye out, cut your hand off, cut your foot off, because they are as your soul. Some of y’all are scared to cut off these wicked kids, the wicked wife, the wicked husband. Cut them off, because they’re going to lead you down the rabbit hole of sin.

precepts.why:
“All my familiars watched for my halting”: all my familiars are all my family members, all my kinsmen, all my friends. They watch for my halting, they watch for me to fall, because they hate God’s laws.

“Saying, Peradventure he will be enticed”: hopefully he’ll be enticed by the big butt woman over there. “And we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.” Why revenge? Because they hated God’s law. That is the brother, the son, the daughter, the wife and the friend of Deuteronomy 13:6: the enticer is in your own circle, waiting for you to fall.

“Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father”. God’s laws in Christ will set a man at variance against his father, “and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.” Your enemies will be in your house, first and foremost.

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me”: that’s what Moses warned us about in Deuteronomy 13. “And he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” Some of y’all go out of your way to get your rebellious children from a rebellious wife because you want full custody, and when you get that child back the child says, ‘I don’t want to keep no damn commandments, I want to hang in the streets.’ Now you’re stuck, because you love that child so much, and it was a rebellious child, a hateful child. You women, the same with y’all.

“And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.” If you ain’t willing to put your life on the line and die, Christ said you’re not worthy to be his disciple.

“He that findeth his life shall lose it”: you try to find your life: ‘I want to get my family back, I know they hate God but I want them back, I’m gonna leave the commandments out of love for my wicked kids and my wicked wife or my wicked husband.’ “And he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it”: losing your life means they’re all cut off, the wicked wife is gone, the wicked kids, the wicked husband, the wicked friends that are trying to get you to sin. Lose your life; be willing to go so far as to sacrifice your life in your faith for this truth.

“Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide”: sometimes your friend can go off, a guide can go off. There is always that possibility to stumble in this truth, to fall in this truth, and that’s why you don’t put your 100 percent trust in somebody. “Keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom”: you don’t put all your trust in the woman that lies on your bosom. Samson did, and look what happened to him. It didn’t go well for Samson and it ain’t gonna go well for you either. ‘I’ma tell my wife everything’: you’re simple as hell.

“For the son dishonoureth the father”: some of you love them kids so much and your own kids disrespect you. “The daughter riseth up against her mother”: some of you women know your daughter can’t stand you. “A man’s enemies are the men of his own house”: that’s the same thing Christ said in Matthew 10:36.

“Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy”: a lot of times we read that and say it’s the other nations, but it’s talking about the people in your house who hate God, and hate you for loving God. “When I fall, I shall arise”: they’re waiting for you to fall, and when you fall and stumble in this truth they mock you, but when I fall I shall arise. “When I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me.”

“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him”: we know whatever we do against God’s law we’re going to suffer for it, but we know the Lord is merciful, “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

“Then she that is mine enemy shall see it”: she is your wife. She hated the commandments, and when you fell she wanted you dead, but you rose up, you repented, and she shall see it. “And shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God?” That’s the same thing Job’s wife said: ‘where’s the Lord your God, keeping your damn commandments?’ “Mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.” God says don’t worry, I got her; her judgment is death, I’m going to kill her in time. You simp brothers need to understand it: if these women can’t get their act together, not these lovely women here, God says I’m going to kill her. That ain’t what I said; that’s what the Bible says.

Those men and women that entice you to sin are part of this world. They don’t want to be woken up to God’s light; they don’t want to come out of darkness into the marvellous light. They will fight you, they will kick you, they will call the police on you for trying to get them to keep God’s commandments.

“If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time”: the indiscreet are men and women who don’t keep the commandments. If you’re around them, check your watch, check yourself: what time is it? ‘I’ve been with you two minutes, I got to go.’ You do got something to do, like repent. Leave them. “But be continually among men of understanding.”

These are the type of folks you need to cut off. “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness”: fellowship means friendship. Y’all going to the bar together, hanging out at each other’s house: have no fellowship. “But rather reprove them”: rather correct them.

“For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret.” Some of the vile filth they do in secret: threesomes and foursomes, wife swapping. In one of our camps, sister A and sister B, friends who love ‘the sisterhood’, got to talking about what each one’s man was like. A month went by, two months of that type of conversation, and then one of the sisters said, how about we switch. That should have been a red flag. One husband was down for it already, because that’s what they did in the world; the other was reluctant at first, but then he did it, and they switched partners, four people in one bed. You’d be shocked at the things that have occurred, and you know where to throw them: out.

Running with the man bragging about who he did yesterday is the unfruitful work of darkness, and what do you think is going to end up happening? You’re going to be seduced. That’s how a lot of you brothers end up back in the world: hanging around the wrong people. You hang around five dummies, you gonna be the sixth. Sisters, you hang around five hoes, you’re gonna be the sixth. ‘I’m not a hoe, I just hang around them’: you’re simple as hell.

“Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.” Sisters send messages asking, I got some friends in the world, is it okay if I hang out with them? Those messages get ignored and deleted. If you’ve been with us a year you can’t be that stupid, to ask if you can hang out with friends in the world that you know are drug dealers and drug users.

In Old Town, at a hotel, an LGBT dude came up talking about ‘what do you want for dinner’. You’re fooling nobody. You’re a Transformer, you are not a woman: more than meets the eye. They want you to join in their delusion: call me her, use my pronoun. So to be a part of this world means to be an enemy of God.

“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world”: like that rap music some of y’all still listen to, all that worldly stuff some of y’all are still involved in and don’t want to let go. “If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” The love of the Father is not in you. Yes, it is hard, but that’s why repenting is a daily thing, and we got to study, pray, apply daily.

“I pray for them”: Christ is praying for the twelve. “I pray not for the world”: he doesn’t pray for the world, meaning the Israelites that are outside. “But for them which thou hast given me”: that was the twelve first and foremost, and those disciples at the time. “And all mine are thine”: all mine meaning my disciples.

“Holy Father, keep through thine own name”: letting you know the Father and the Son are two different powers. “That they may be one, as we are”: one meaning on one accord, in agreement. It ain’t talking about one person.

“None of them is lost, but the son of perdition”: that’s Judas Iscariot. He was the son of perdition, the betrayer.

“I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them”. When you get into this Bible and start applying it, expect to be hated. That’s the ADL read at the beginning of class: they hate our people that are in the scriptures. They ain’t worried about Christians; Christians are under delusion. But the Israelites, they hate our guts, and they push the term ‘hate group’ on us, when in reality they’re the hate group.

“Because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world”, “but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” So when 1 John says love not the world, it’s talking about the evil: the men and women that live in the world. They are evil, and that’s what God wants us to understand.

“Neither pray I for these alone”: not just the twelve disciples and the disciples that were with them, “but for them also which shall believe on me through their word”. That’s us today, you and me.

“That they all may be one”: meaning perfectly joined in unity, one mind, “as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.” Christ is showing that the twelve are going to have one mind and always be together.

sense.text:
This goes with cutting off the family members or friends that cause you to sin. “Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness”: it seems like a contradiction, Christ telling us to make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness. Mammon is wealth regarded as an evil influence or false object of worship; in the Bible it is the term for riches, often used for the debasing influence of material wealth. The mammon of unrighteousness is the people in the world that don’t believe the truth.

Verses 1 through 8 are the parable of an unjust steward that dealt unwisely and got fired from his job, and he had to deal right with people so they would help him. So Christ says make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness, “that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.”

precepts.why:
Here is the precept for understanding why: “And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falleth, he shall find a stay.” When you fall you shall find help.

So if you deal right with people on your job, when you need help they will help you. But if you’re on your job acting like a nuka, nobody is gonna help you when you need it.

sense.text: Don’t get trapped serving this world for money. “No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. Serving mammon means you got that covetous spirit: everything you do is about money. You can’t serve two gods; when you’re serving mammon, meaning riches, that’s your god. “Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” You got to love one and hate the other. Make your choice.

precepts.why:
This is for you brothers who put your job ahead of God’s work. “They shall not be sought for in publick counsel, nor sit high in the congregation”: don’t look for rank if your job is your first priority.

“They shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment”: don’t ask why you don’t understand certain judgments. You’ve not been around, you’ve not studied, you’ve not prayed nor applied, but you’ve gone to work sun up to sundown every day. “They cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken”: when we’re going over parables you’re nowhere around.

“But they will maintain the state of the world”: your whole life is maintaining the United States of America. “And all their desire is in the work of their craft.”

sense.text: Before talking about Lazarus and the lake of fire, these scriptures lead up to it. This chapter is talking about a servant named Eliakim: “I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah”. Eliakim the son of Hilkiah is symbolic for the coming Messiah, whom the world calls Christ.

“And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder”: this is Christ. Why does it say the house of David? Because it’s referring to the twelve tribes of Israel; that’s the house of David. The house of David ain’t talking about the Philistines. It is the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.why:
The precept about the house of David: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. The tabernacle of David is the house of David, the twelve tribes of Israel.

This makes reference to Cornelius and his kinsfolk and friends repenting: he was bringing back the northern kingdom with Judah, bringing back the twelve tribes again. That’s what the whole chapter is about, going back to Acts 10, and Christianity still hasn’t figured that out.

Christ is the one that has the key of David: “These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth”. The key of David is the uniting of the twelve tribes of Israel. He’s the one that opens understanding or shuts understanding, and when he shuts, no man can open it. Once you’re out of his truth, you’re out, like Judas: there was no coming back for him.

“Behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”: the open door is for us to repent, and no man can shut it. I don’t care how much missile technology Esau got, he cannot shut the door to us repenting. “For thou hast a little strength”: the little strength is the word of God, the Bible, “and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name”: we are not to deny the Son of God.

“Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet”. Can’t no man shut that down. He said I open and I shut; you can’t stop this.

“Woe unto you, lawyers!”: the lawyers were the Levites that followed the scribes, the Sadducees and the Pharisees. “For ye have taken away the key of knowledge”: see, that is what the key of David is. “Ye entered not in yourselves”: you ain’t coming into New Jerusalem. “And them that were entering in ye hindered”: you offended them, you taught lies to keep them from repenting. You ain’t getting into New Jerusalem, the kingdom of heaven, whatever you call it.

So the key of David is the key of knowledge.

sense.text: Now we’re getting into the topic: we’re going to talk about death. “Why died I not from the womb?” Why didn’t I die as a baby? “Why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why didn’t I die when I was born? Job caught hell, so he’s upset.

“Why did the knees prevent me?” Why my mama’s knees, my family: how your mama bounces you on her knees as a baby to keep you up and keep you going. “Or why the breasts that I should suck?” Why was she giving me her breasts to feed me, breastfeed me, nurture me.
“For now should I have lain still and been quiet”: if my mama didn’t do that, I would have laid still and dead. “I should have slept: then had I been at rest”: if I died I would have been at rest.
At rest “with kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves; Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver”.
“An hidden untimely birth”: that’s stillborn deaths. Why was I not like that, “as infants which never saw light.”
There, when you’re dead, “the wicked cease from troubling” people, “and there the weary be at rest.”
“There the prisoners rest together” in the grave. “They hear not the voice of the oppressor”: there’s no oppressor when you’re dead.

“The small and great are there”: the small of the nations are there and the greatest of the nations are there, “and the servant is free from his master.”

Job is explaining death. When you die your soul, your spirit, is at rest. You’re not being thrown in the middle of the earth with Satan saying gotcha now, gotcha, gotcha, poking you with a pitchfork. But when Christ comes, that’s another matter.

This is what we have to be mindful of: the second coming. There’s a lot of things that’s going to happen when Christ returns. “I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.”

Do you see what Christ said? “The keys of hell and of death”: letting you know it’s two different things there, hell and death. Remember at the beginning of the lesson where we talked about if you don’t cut them off you’re going to be cast into hell, hell fire, everlasting fire? Did y’all forget already? Highlight that: hell, hell fire, everlasting fire. Christ says here he has the keys of hell and death. Remember what he said earlier: what I open no man can shut, what I shut no man can open.

Pay close attention. We’re talking about the second coming. Remember Christ said I have the keys of hell and death: what do you mean by that? Read. “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”: Michael stands for the Israelites. He don’t stand for all nations; he only stands for the children of thy people.

“And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time”. Pause there and think about that a second: what could he be talking about? He’s talking about war like you’ve never seen. It’s always been war on this earth, but this type of war has never ever happened. That’s a day of trouble such as has never been.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book”: everyone that shall be found written in the Book of Life.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Now we know our spirits don’t stay in the ground; our spirits are not in the earth, we go up before the Lord. So now we understand it: this is in the heavens. Being awakened from the dust of the earth is symbolic for the heavenly realm, where our souls rest.

“Some to everlasting life”: some of us are going to be waking up to everlasting life; that’s the resurrection of the dead. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: some souls are going to be awakened to shame and everlasting contempt.

Right now, when we pass away, Christ has not opened that up yet; we all rest. But when he returns he’s going to open it up, because he’s got the keys to hell and death. He knows who’s going to be for everlasting life and who’s destined for contempt and everlasting damnation.

precepts.why:
Here is the war such as never was. “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet”: that’s only done by a nuclear missile. “And their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the Lord shall be among them”.

That right there is what’s going to happen in this third world war when Christ returns. That’s what it means, a time of trouble such as never was.

The precept to Zechariah 14:12. It talks about missiles in the Bible; the Bible talks about everything. “Behold, I have created the smith”: the smith there is Oppenheimer. “The smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” That’s what Oppenheimer said when he created the atom bomb: now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.

Then we read in 2 Esdras 11 where it said ‘the end of this your time’ shall come through them. These are the people that are going to bring about the end of this civilization that we see today.

Our spirits don’t stay in the ground. “Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?” So when we go back to Daniel 12:2, “many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”, we know our spirits are not in the earth. We go up before the Lord.

Remember when Samuel died, and King Saul said to the witch, summon Samuel, tell me what you see? That’s why I need y’all to study, pray, apply. “And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.” Ascending, ascending, ascending out of the earth. Who knows the spirit of man that goeth upward: that’s what we just read in Ecclesiastes.

That everlasting contempt. Pay very close attention. “Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice”: everybody that died is going to hear the Lord’s voice. “And shall come forth; they that have done good”, that have kept God’s commandments, “unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil”, like your mama and your daddy, “unto the resurrection of damnation.” Of what? Of damnation. Damn nation.

That goes with Daniel 12:2: some awake to everlasting life, the resurrection of life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt, the resurrection of damnation.

Don’t be deceived by Israelite camps or churches that say it don’t matter what sin you do, just say you believe and you’re going to be all right. All I can do is warn you. They’ve got slander and hatred and they think they’re going to get the kingdom.

“Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.” The blasphemy against the Holy Ghost is when you know these scriptures and you reject these scriptures.

“And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him”: like Paul, he spoke against Christ. You do foolish things, say foolish things, before you repent. “But whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost”, you learn this gospel and then you reject this gospel, “it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.”

Do y’all see that? Don’t be deceived thinking you’re going to be wicked as hell and you’re just going to come back as a baby born in the kingdom. Some wake to shame and everlasting contempt.

sense.text: “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works”: his works is the commandments, “and by faith, whereby ye have believed”. Y’all see the part where it says works and faith? Works and faith.

“Shall be preserved from the said perils”: shall be preserved from danger, destruction, “and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders”: that’s the wilderness. “For I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.”

“Then shall they be in pitiful case”: who is he talking about? Those “which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.” Shall what? Shall dwell in torments.

“For such as in their life have received benefits”: you got the best job, you make the most money, you’re a billionaire, millionaire, you good. “And have not known me”: have not known the Lord by keeping his commandments and the faith of Jesus.

“And they that have lothed my law”: many hated my law, “while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it”. You despised keeping God’s commandments by repentance.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” Did y’all see that right there? That’s what Christ was saying when he said I’ve got the keys of hell and death.

Right now, when we die, like brothers that died yesterday or last week, they rest. They had rest, and we know they’re going to get everlasting life, because they were keeping the commandments. But your mamas and daddies, sisters and brothers who were breaking God’s law, gave you the finger, hated the Bible: they died, and when the Lord returns they’re going to get their contempt and everlasting shame.

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept to works and faith. You got Christians going, no, it’s not by works. They don’t understand what they’re saying: they’re telling you you can be an adulterer, a homosexual, a thief and a liar and a murderer and still get the kingdom of heaven on earth.

“Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” See that: the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus. That’s the works and the faith of 2 Esdras 9:7, by which they that are saved escape.

sense.text:
I wanted to preach up this parable with those scriptures. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. Let’s see who this rich man is. You know some of your preachers look like that.

Sometimes we read about the rich man and we don’t realize Israelites were rich. Some of them, not all of them. Nicodemus was rich; Joseph of Arimathea was rich; remember the young man that was rich, and Christ said sell all that you got and give to the poor, and he went away sorrowful; Zacchaeus, who was a tax collector, was rich; Paul was rich at one time. These rich men are the type of rich people amongst us that you see today.
“And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores”. Who is this beggar? The beggar is the one the Lord lifts up from the dunghill to set among princes.

“And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: that’s the little benefits we get in society. “Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” Who are these dogs? Write this down: the dogs cover two things. The dogs are both other nations and wicked Israelites, and it is proven from the scriptures.

A lot of our people live in America, we’re scattered worldwide, and a large proportion of us live on the continent of Africa. The dogs licking the sores of Lazarus is the nations taking our wealth and our riches.

Think about it: you have a black community, a black and Latino community. These nations always set up shop where we live, get all the money they can get from us, and then take it back to their people. We don’t reap the benefits of nothing. This is what the story of Lazarus is about.

And remember, these dogs feed off of our people, the poor of our people. That’s what they do.
“And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: Lazarus dies, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”. Abraham’s bosom is paradise. “The rich man also died, and was buried”.

“And in hell”: at the beginning of the lesson it talked about hell being everlasting fire, remember that. “He lift up his eyes, being in torments”. Being in what? Torment. Now remember, that torment comes when Christ returns.

All this is spiritual. We know once the bombs hit, brothers and sisters, your flesh is gone instantly, but your spirit stays around. “And seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom”: Lazarus is with him.

“And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.” See that: I am tormented in this flame. This flame, we know, is the spiritual side of it, because the physical, your flesh, is gone already. But your spirit, the real you, that’s what we read in Daniel 12: everlasting shame and contempt.

“But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”. Remember in the book of Esdras the Bible said they received benefits: ‘such as in their life have received benefits’. “And likewise Lazarus evil things”: evil things, poverty, oppression. “But now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.” Lazarus, which represents the repentant, is comforted, but now is your turn to be tormented. That’s the same shall know it after death by pain.

“And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot”: there’s nobody that can get over there to you. This is the spiritual realm. In the spiritual realm it’s not permitted for us to even go to you; we can’t get there even if we wanted to. “Neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence”: neither can you come from there to us. This is all in the spirit realm.

Abraham will literally see them being tormented, but the gulf is fixed: they are in the spirit realm being tormented while Abraham is in the kingdom of God with Christ, and there’s nothing that can be done. We can’t go to the spirit world and bring you alive.

“Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house”: send Lazarus to my father’s house, “For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

“Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets”. This is how you know the rich man is Israel: they have who? Moses. “Let them hear them”: let them hear what Moses and the prophets said; that way they could avoid this place.

“And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t even believe if somebody rises from the dead.

Some of y’all, even in here, think if your parents see some wonder they’re going to believe. No: if they were wicked in the past, they’re going to be wicked today.

precepts.why: We’re going to talk about the rich man. “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” This letter is addressed to the twelve tribes.

Still addressed to the twelve tribes. “Go to now, ye rich men”: it’s addressing the rich men of the twelve tribes of Israel. This goes with some of your athletes, your actors, your entertainers.

“Weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you”: when he says weep and howl for your misery, he’s saying you better repent. “Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten. Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you”.

Sometimes we read about the rich man and don’t realize Israelites were rich. The rich man of Luke 16 is a rich man of Israel.

A certain beggar: who is this beggar? “He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory”. Dunghill means doo-doo; y’all know, s-h-i-t.

That precept right there goes with the beggar in Luke 16:20. The beggar is the poor of Israel that the Lord raises up out of the dust to inherit the throne of glory.

The dogs are other nations, and here’s the proof. About Egypt: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” So God is calling the Egyptians dogs.

“Moab is my washpot”: that’s why they’re always in the laundromats. “Over Edom will I cast out my shoe”: you know how you throw your shoe at a dog. Down South we love to throw our shoes at a dog, because they ain’t right, trying to sneak in the house and eat somebody’s food. “Over Philistia will I triumph”: Philistia is Palestine, the Palestinians.

Remember the dogs licked the sores of Lazarus: that’s the nations taking our wealth and our riches. Everything we’re about to read, the majority of it, 99.9, they get from the continent of Africa.

“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: The merchandise of gold”: they get that from Africa. “and precious stones”, from Africa, “and of pearls”, from Africa, “and fine linen”, “and purple”, from Africa, “and silk”, from Africa and Madagascar, “and scarlet”, “and all manner vessels of ivory”, “and of brass, and iron, and marble”, “And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat”, “and sheep, and horses”, “and slaves, and souls of men”: all from Africa.

These are the things they do to our people, the Shemites who live on the continent. These are the dogs that lick the sores: they take, they take, they take from us. When we’ve been through Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone, this is what you’ll see: sit down in a restaurant to eat, you’ll always see an Edomite with our people. They have deceived our people into thinking they’re going to benefit from a business. They just put the blacks as the face over the company, but behind the scenes it’s always the white man reaping all the financial benefits. They’ll give the blacks maybe a dollar more here and a dollar there, and our people really think they have made it. Some of our people will curse you, spit at you, look down on you, because they are working with the white man. We saw it in Sierra Leone and Nigeria, the same thing: I am with the white man, my brother, he is God, you are nothing.

They hire Africans, and a lot of them are our people, and pay them pennies on the dollar to do the mining and things of that nature. The map of Africa: mine, mine, mine, for the diamonds in South Africa, the gold in Ghana. This is what Esau and the nations do, because it ain’t just Esau: it’s China doing it, the Arabs doing it too. And Esau behind the scenes is filthy rich. They are the dogs.

How do you know the white man’s a dog? Here’s another scripture proof that they’re the dogs Christ was talking about. “And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid”: Christ couldn’t be hid, he was so famous. “For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation”: she was a Greek, meaning she was Syrian and lived in Phenicia. “And she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.”

“But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.” Cast it unto who? The dogs. The churches never explained it: he’s insulting her. There’s an s: he didn’t say dog, he said dogs, for her and her people, her daughter, her people. Dogs is plural. Nobody in Christianity wants to stay on that; they want to run by it. No, let’s pause right there and talk about this. This loving Jesus called her dogs, not just her, but her daughter’s a dog and her people are dogs. That’s your mama a dog; that’s what the Son of God is saying right there. That’s what you got to do on the street: don’t let them run by that.

“And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.” What did she do? Yes, Lord. She admitted she’s a dog. Y’all try to get the white man to admit that. “And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.” That’s what you got to stress: for this saying. What saying? That she was a dog and her people are dogs. No Christian wants to deal with that. They want you to keep reading and just run; read on, read quick. No, we’re going to read this slow. The other nations are dogs.

Some brothers use that and say a dog is a female, b-i-t-c-h. You brothers know: we got to use the words in the Bible. She’s a dog, her child is a dog, her people, all the men in her nation, are dogs. They’ll understand. Don’t try to be slick and do your own thing talking about a dog is a b-i-t-c-h, so Christ called her a b-i-t-c-h. No.

Not only are the other nations dogs, but rich and wicked Israelites are dogs. “His watchmen are blind”: the white man has set up watchmen, and the watchmen he set up are our people, as taskmasters. They can’t understand, they can’t see the scriptures.

“They are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark”: a dog barking is meant to warn you. These dumb dogs, these Pharisees, cannot warn the people of impending doom. “Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”: always want money, money, money. “And they are shepherds that cannot understand”: shepherds that can’t understand the word of God. “They all look to their own way, every one for his gain”: for his own gain, money, money, money, “from his quarter”: from wherever his church is set up, that’s what it means, from his quarter.

Here’s the precept of his watchmen. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

So who set the scribes and Pharisees up in their positions? The Romans. These Pharisees and Sadducees, these religious leaders, were the watchmen, the dumb dogs of Isaiah 56:10.

We see that Christ called them dogs; here’s another one. “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me”. When Christ was on the cross it wasn’t just the Romans that were around him. You had the scribes and Pharisees saying, he calls on Elijah, let’s see if he’s going to be saved: they were making mockery of the Son of God while he was on the cross.

“They pierced my hands and my feet”: that was the Romans. “I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.”

“Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog.” The dog that had power at that time was with the Romans. You had these wicked scribes and Pharisees doing the will of Rome, so they all fall in that dog category.

What has that got to do with us today? Today our people do the bidding of the Christian church: the Vatican, the Protestant Christians. They are dogs. Your famous, world-renowned Christian pastors are dogs: their bishops, the deacons, the ushers, the deaconesses, all dogs. Give me ten of your earnings: all of them are dogs.

And don’t forget the wicked Israelites today, the ones with the mouth speaking evil against their brothers. They’re dogs too, because eventually they’re going to join with Esau to come against us. I’m talking to you: you are a dog.

More precepts on dogs. “There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” Now watch what Moses calls the whore and the sodomite. “Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore, or the price of a dog, into the house of the Lord thy God for any vow: for even both these are abomination unto the Lord thy God.”

Don’t bring the hire of a whore: you make money off a whore, the Lord said I don’t want that money. Neither the price of a dog: that sodomite, you made money off that, don’t bring that money into the temple. It’s calling our people in them lifestyles dogs.

We’re still talking about dogs, and remember, these dogs feed off of our people, the poor of our people. “For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ”: that’s you men and women listening now that claim you’ve repented. “They are again entangled therein”: you get entangled in your former sins, “and overcome”: you get overcome by your former sins. “The latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them”: you left the commandments of God.

“But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb”: watch what it calls you. “The dog is turned to his own vomit again”: you’re a dog that has returned to your own vomit again. “And the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire”: you’re a pig.

“Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” The only way you get into the gates of the city, we got to keep the commandments.

“For without are dogs”: outside New Jerusalem are dogs, that’s the other nations, “and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.” So you ain’t getting in.

We’ve read all these precepts to help us understand the parable of Lazarus. Now that we went through them, it helps us understand what Christ is talking about with the dogs that licked his sores.

Here’s the evidence that they won’t be persuaded though one rose from the dead. “Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” Remember in history, Christ raised Lazarus from the dead.

precepts.why:

“Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” Didn’t we just read that in Isaiah 66? Their worm, the soul, your soul, dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

“And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life”, better to enter without that foot, “than having two feet to be cast into hell”, than to have your friend or family member with you and be cast into hell, “into the fire that never shall be quenched.” Again: “Where their worm dieth not”, where their soul dieth not, “and the fire is not quenched.”

“And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.”

sense.text:
Pay close attention: this is not hallucinating or imagining; it’s what the Bible is saying.

precepts.why: Worshipping the beast and his image and receiving his mark in your hand or your forehead is the same thing we read in Second Thessalonians. It just uses different words but it’s talking about the same thing: “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” What is unrighteousness? Sin.

The precept to the smoke going up for ever and ever is Isaiah 34, read from verse 4 because at the beginning of the lesson we talked about Idumea, Edom.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: this is World War Three, Armageddon, the return of the King. “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down”: all their host means the satellites, the missiles, everything that’s up there; they’re gonna fall, “as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.”

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: this is Christ. “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: who’s Idumea? Your brothers. “And upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” The scholar we read at the beginning of the lesson understood it: he said this is the white man. You got a problem with the white man? We know inside there’s a Christian sitting there; you got to rebuke that in the name of the Lord.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah.” Bozrah was one of the capital cities of Edom. See that it compares the destruction to a sacrifice; that’s what we read about earlier in today’s lesson. “And a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: it’s going to be a great slaughter, a sacrifice.

“And the unicorns shall come down with them”: the unicorn means the rhinoceros, and it’s talking about nations of men, “and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.” Why? “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” Zion is the Israelites, and the controversy is who the land of Israel belongs to.

“And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.” The land of Idumea is talking about Babylon the great. Here’s the proof: “It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever.” Didn’t we just read that in Revelation 14? It’s saying the same thing: up for ever, a long time. “From generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.”

precepts.why:

sense.text:
We want victory; we want to overcome.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth”: in this time, it’s prophesied, we must be in pain and labour to bring forth. Part of that pain means you might have to cut some of your loved ones off, the ones telling you don’t keep the Commandments. It hurts not talking to your mama no more; it hurts not being with your wife or your husband no more. But those of the spirit saying ‘I’m not keeping the Commandments and neither are you’ got to be cut off. Labour means work: you gotta work to bring forth this truth.

“O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail.” A woman in travail has birthing pains: they may be spaced an hour apart, then thirty minutes apart, then minutes, then seconds, then the baby comes out. Likewise in this truth you’re gonna have days of pain, problems in this world, issues coming up, spaced years apart, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes apart; and then that destruction, and we are delivered.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”: that Babylon is Babylon the great. “There shalt thou be delivered.” That’s the evidence: we weren’t delivered from ancient Babylon by the Lord, but we’re going to be delivered from this Babylon. “There the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.” That didn’t happen in ancient Babylon: Persia conquered them, and we went into the Persian captivity. So this is about the Lord redeeming us.

“Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled”: all nations are against us. Let Israel be defiled; let them sin, let them sin, let them die. “And let our eye look upon Zion”: they took the land.

“But they know not the thoughts of the Lord”: these nations don’t understand the thoughts of God Almighty, “neither understand they his counsel”: neither do they understand the Bible; that’s his counsel. “For he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.”

“Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron”: I will make you powerful as iron, “and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people.” Y’all don’t want this victory? I want this victory: we gonna beat in pieces many people.

“And I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord”: their wealth, the wealth of the nations, “and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.” We’re gonna take all their wealth and consecrate it to the Lord.

“Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops”: gather yourselves together. “He hath laid siege against us”: these nations laid siege against us at one time and they still do today. “They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek”: they beat the judge of Israel; they beat Christ.

“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.” That is talking about Christ.

“Therefore will he give them up”: that’s talking about us, “until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren”, that’s you and me, “shall return unto the children of Israel.” We’re going to return as the Israelites. Americans no more; we ain’t Puerto Ricans, we ain’t Haitians, we ain’t Dominicans: we are the Israelites. That’s what he’s saying.

“And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God”: that’s the Father, God. “And they shall abide: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth”: Christ is going to be great unto the ends of the earth.

“And this man shall be the peace”: Christ is the peace. “When the Assyrian shall come into our land”, when they took over Jerusalem, “and when he shall tread in our palaces”, over on this side of the earth.

“Then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men.” Seven shepherds and eight principal men: that’s a total of fifteen men.

“And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword”: the sword is the word of God. “And the land of Nimrod”: that’s Babylon the great. Remember Nimrod’s kingdom was called Babel.

“Thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.” He, meaning Christ, delivers us. Teaching the Bible we can only wake up our people and prophesy; so the Lord said, I got to come save you.

After Christ delivers us: “And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the Lord”: we gonna be everywhere, “as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men.” We gotta wait on the Lord.

“And the remnant of Jacob”, that’s you and me, “shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest.” What do the beasts of the field do when they see a lion but run? “As a young lion among the flocks of sheep”: what can sheep do to a lion? Nothing but be food. “Who, if he go through”, when we go through these nations, “both treadeth down”, we’re gonna tread them down, “and teareth in pieces”, we gonna tear them in pieces, “and none can deliver”: nobody gonna save these nations.
“Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off.” He’s going to give us power.

“I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds.” He’s gonna throw down all the strongholds of the nations.

“And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand.” Believe it or not, witchcraft is practiced here in America. Witchcraft is the TV, the internet; the technology is all witchcraft. “And thou shalt have no more soothsayers.”

“Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee”: all these images here in this country gonna be thrown down. “And thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands”: no more worshipping idols.

“And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen”, upon the nations, “such as they have not heard.” That’s what Daniel 12 was saying, the same thing.

precepts.why: The precept to prove they smote the judge of Israel, so y’all know it ain’t made up: “And they spit upon him”, they spit upon the Lord, “and took the reed, and smote him on the head”, hit him on his head. “And after that they had mocked him”: they mocked the Son of God, our Messiah, our King, our Lord, our almighty God. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” That’s what was wanted: the Prince of Peace. This man shall be the peace.

What is that sword they shall waste the land of Assyria with? “For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit”: soul and spirit, because these words are spiritual.

“And of the joints and marrow”: joints and marrow, that’s physical. After New Jerusalem is set up and the Lord sends us against these nations, remember what we read: we’re going to beat people into pieces. That’s the joints and marrow part, the physical.

“And is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Only the Bible can do that.

“The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might”: the nations are gonna see and be confounded at the might of the twelve tribes of Israel. “They shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf.”

That’s why the Lord says he’s gonna do a marvelous work in your day, such as you’ve never heard. That’s what the Lord gonna do: vengeance upon the heathen such as they have not heard.

sense.text: “In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them”, he that is feeble amongst us, “at that day shall be as David; and the house of David”, the 144, “shall be as God”, as God on earth, “as the angel of the Lord before them.” We gonna be as an angel of God before them.

“For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.” Fear not, brothers; fear not, sisters. Fear not, fear not.

“Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel.” Notice he calls us a worm, because we’re in these weak bodies; our soul is even as a worm. Remember what was said about the wicked, where their worm dieth not; so it’s calling us that worm.

“I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.” He said it four or five times: I will help you, I will help you, I will help you.

“Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth”: power. He’s gonna give us power on the earth like it’s never been seen before. “Thou shalt thresh the mountains”: we’re gonna thresh the mountains, meaning the governments, “and beat them small”: we’re gonna beat the governments of the world small. “And shalt make the hills as chaff”: we’re gonna make the smaller governments as chaff.

“Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away”: when we fan these nations the wind shall carry them away, “and the whirlwind shall scatter them: and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, and shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.” Rejoice, brothers; rejoice, sisters.

precepts.why: “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

What is fear? This explains it. ‘I’m scared to teach, I’m fearful’: what does that break down to? “And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?” Fear breaks down to having no faith. He has not given us that spirit. So when Isaiah says fear thou not, it is saying have faith.
